subsystems.name: Cruise and orbit-insertion propulsion
subsystems.role: carries the craft from Earth to Saturn and slows it enough to be captured around Enceladus itself.
parts: chemical main engine and propellant tanks
reaction wheels and thrusters for attitude control

subsystems.name: Plume-sampling system
subsystems.role: captures fresh ocean material during fast passes through the plume without destroying the fragile organics.
parts: inlet or collector that faces the relative wind
transfer mechanism to sealed sample cells

subsystems.name: Lander
subsystems.role: sets down on the south polar terrain and holds the instruments steady for a long surface campaign.
parts: sampling scoop or collector for plume fallout

subsystems.name: Life-detection instrument suite
subsystems.role: searches for patterns of organic molecules and their distributions that living processes would produce.
parts: separation channel for amino acids and their chirality

subsystems.name: Power, thermal and communications
subsystems.role: keeps instruments warm and sends results back across more than a billion kilometres.
parts: radioisotope or large solar power source

subsystems.name: Contamination control
subsystems.role: prevents Earth microbes and Earth organics from being mistaken for Enceladus life.
parts: witness plates that record any contamination

buildSteps.title: Choose the biosignature pattern
buildSteps.detail: Decide in advance which measurable distributions — such as a preference for one molecular handedness, or chain lengths that don't match random chemistry — would count as evidence, because that choice fixes the instruments.

buildSteps.title: Design the combined orbiter-lander
buildSteps.detail: One spacecraft must fly a multi-year cruise, orbit a small icy moon and then land on it, so mass, power, communications and landing loads are traded against each other from the start.

buildSteps.title: Build and qualify the instruments
buildSteps.detail: Each instrument is tested for sensitivity to trace organics, then shaken, baked in thermal vacuum and irradiated to prove it survives launch and the space environment.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the flight system
buildSteps.detail: Instruments are integrated into the lander deck and orbiter bus, and the plume-sampling path is tested with particle beams at the speeds it will meet in flight.

buildSteps.title: Sterilise and clean
buildSteps.detail: The whole spacecraft is assembled in clean rooms and subjected to heat and chemical sterilisation so it carries as little Earth biology as possible to the target.

buildSteps.title: Launch and cruise
buildSteps.detail: After launch, the craft spends years looping through planetary gravity assists to reach the Saturn system with enough propellant left to stop there.

buildSteps.title: Enter Enceladus orbit
buildSteps.detail: A Saturn tour uses flybys of the moons to shape the orbit, ending in capture around Enceladus itself.

buildSteps.title: Fly the plume campaign
buildSteps.detail: Repeated close passes at kilometres per second sweep fresh plume particles into the collector, which is then sealed and analysed.

buildSteps.title: Land and sample the surface
buildSteps.detail: The craft descends to the south polar terrain in low gravity, collects plume fallout that settles on the ground near the vents, and runs the life-detection suite over a long surface phase.

prerequisites.tech: Discovery of the plume and subsurface ocean
prerequisites.why: Cassini found the vents, flew through the plume and showed it carries salts, organics and hydrogen — the evidence that makes the whole mission worth flying.

prerequisites.tech: Small-moon orbit insertion and tour design
prerequisites.why: Cassini's Saturn tour proved that gravity assists can deliver a spacecraft into orbit around a moon with limited propellant.

prerequisites.tech: High-speed particle capture that preserves organics
prerequisites.why: comet dust was captured and returned through low-density aerogel, but the plume impact speeds are far higher and the molecules of interest are far more fragile.
laboratory instruments can detect trace amino acids and handedness, but shrinking them onto a spacecraft without carrying their own contamination is unsolved.

prerequisites.tech: Long-life power and thermal control at Saturn
prerequisites.why: radioisotope power and multilayer insulation have kept spacecraft alive for over a decade in the outer solar system.

pathway.milestone: concept studies for a combined orbiter-lander, assessed as a candidate flagship mission in recent planetary-science decadal planning
pathway.unlocks: a defined instrument set and a credible architecture that engineers can cost and improve.

pathway.milestone: a smaller, cheaper plume-flyby mission to characterise the plume chemistry more thoroughly
pathway.unlocks: the organic inventory and background knowledge an Orbilander needs to interpret its own results.

pathway.milestone: the Orbilander itself, launched and flown to the Saturn system
pathway.unlocks: fresh ocean material analysed for biosignature patterns, on the surface and from orbit.

pathway.milestone: a melt probe that descends from the surface ice into the ocean
pathway.unlocks: direct sampling of the habitable environment rather than its ejected debris.
